newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan Dec jobless seen flat-Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan Dec jobless seen flat-Reuters poll.

text.p: The following Reuters poll of economists gives projections for Taiwan's December jobless rate, which is due for official release at 0300 GMT on January 23 by the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.

Economists said they expected December joblessness to remain at comparatively high levels because of the disappointingly slow pace of the current recovery, resulting in slower-than-expected new employment.
"Domestic recovery has just begun and it's not strong enough to have many new plants opening," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
Taiwan's jobless rate held close to 1.5 percent in 1991-1994, but rose to 1.79 percent in 1995 and has pushed above 3.0 percent in August, September and October 1996.

Officials have attributed the shift to higher jobless levels to basic changes in Taiwan's economy -- a broad move toward service-oriented industry from the lower-tier, labour-intensive manufacturing that had engendered the island's dramatic economic development in the 1970s and 1980s.
